transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The U.S. military says it's disabled a commercial ship in the Gulf of Oman as it attempted
to break the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports.
The strike comes as the Trump administration has been noncommittal on its next move, nine
months into the U.S. war in Iran.
John Piers, Kat Lonsdorf, has more.
U.S. Central Command says a military aircraft fired "precision munitions" at a merchant
vessel attempting to leave an Iranian port.
CENTCOM said in a statement that the civilian crew of the ship was unharmed.
The U.S. military has been blocking Iranian ports since April.
It temporarily lifted the blockade over the summer during talks with Tehran, but resumed
it in July.
This strike was the 15th ship the U.S. has disclosed disabling during its blockade, including
at least two strikes that have resulted in the killing of multiple crew members.
President Trump has wavered on what to do next in Iran, suggesting on Thanksgiving Day
that the end of the war will be "whenever he decides."
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
In Israel, political opposition leaders are making progress toward forming a new government
that would unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
NPR's Daniel Estrin has more from Tel Aviv.
One Israeli opposition leader says a new government could be formed next week, with centrist
Gadi Eizenkot as Prime Minister.
Eizenkot is expected to form a diverse coalition, from left-wing to center-right to hard-right
parties.
Reuven Khazan, Politics Professor at Hebrew University.
They're all over the map politically.
The only thing that keeps them together is that they are opposed to Netanyahu and they
want to remove him from office.
A new government could include one of Netanyahu's traditional allies, an ultra-Orthodox Jewish
party, and it could rely on the support of a moderate Arab-Islamist party.
Opposition leaders are rushing to announce a government soon.
They're worried Netanyahu could spark a new war with Iran, which could complicate efforts
to remove him from power.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The powerful coastal storm that ran up the east coast yesterday is winding down, and
power is slowly being restored to the hundreds of thousands of customers who lost it during
those storms.
In Baltimore, Magdalena Stellilesco says it was a different kind of a holiday, a day that
was also her 11-year-old son's birthday, as they lost power yesterday on the holiday.
We did Thanksgiving at candlelight.
We had guests over.
We kept on going, celebrated his birthday as well at candlelight.
So it was, yeah, something different.
The weather also led travel disruptions down trees and water rescues from Virginia to New
York City, where the annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed because of high winds
for the first time and will be held tomorrow.
But the delay left performers and marching bands scrambling to find ways to stay in New
York to perform on the new parade date.
You're listening to NPR News.
The United Nations food agencies say hunger is expected to get worse in 16 countries over
the next six months, with five countries at the greatest risk.
Four-torn Sudan and South Sudan, Yemen, Somalia and northern Nigeria.
All five appeared on the list for the past four years.
The Palestinian territory was moved down a level following the October 2025 ceasefire
in Gaza, but 67 percent of Gaza's population still faces crisis-level hunger.
The blue wave of this year's midterms has implications for the 2028 presidential election
as well, having swept competitive Secretary of State races this year.
Democrats will oversee the voting process in virtually every swing state.
NPR's Miles Parks has more.
If President Trump is hoping to change how people vote in the 2028 election, he will
have few allies at the state level.
Democrats will oversee the voting process for every presidential battleground state except
for North Carolina, after Democrats flipped the office of Secretary of State in Georgia
and Ohio and took the governor's mansion in Texas.
Even Democrats in Arizona and Nevada fended off challenges from Republicans who falsely
claimed that the 2020 election was stolen from Trump.
That was another trend in this year's midterms.
According to national tracking by the advocacy group States United Action, there will be
fewer election-denying politicians in office next year.
Miles Parks, NPR News, Washington.
Budget Airlines' North Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy protection a day after
stopping flights and ticket sales.
The Norwegian airline was founded in 2021 and offered cheap flights from Europe to Asia,
South Africa, and the U.S.
You're listening to NPR News.
